RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the March 20, 2007/Phalguna 29, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Culture; Finance;
Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises; Petroleum and
Natural Gas; Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
Setting up of Airport Development
Centre
*301. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL : Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
undertaking upgradation and modernization
of airports in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether there is any plan to set up
an Airport Development Centre for this
purpose; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Opening of branches of UCBs
†*302. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Reserve Bank of India
is contemplating giving permission to open
more branches of banks to strengthen
Urban Co-operative Banks;
(b) the basis for considering any Urban
Co-operative Bank as a weak bank;
(c) the number of such branches of weak
Urban Co-operative Banks in the country
and the action being taken for improving
their condition; and
(d) by when the permission for opening
new branches would be given?
Maintenance of Tomb of Hasan Khan
Suri
†*303. SHRI ALI ANWAR: Will the
Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Tomb of
Hasan Khan Suri, situated in Sasaram, Bihar
is under maintenance of Archaeological
Survey of India;
(b) if so, the arrangements made by
Government for its proper care and
maintenance;
(c) whether it is also a fact that this
Tomb is in a very dilapidated condition
and Archaeological Survey of India is not
able to look after the same properly; and
(d) if so, whether Government would
issue necessary instructions for its proper
maintenance?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

97
Scrapping of panel recommended by
PESB
*304. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES
AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of occasions on which
PESB's recommended panel had been
scrapped for reasons other than vigilance/
corruption since formation of Public
Enterprises Selection Board (PESB) in
1987; and
(b) the details thereof, year-wise and
unit-wise?
Investment in IT export
*305. SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY :
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
would achieve 75 billion dollar investment
in IT export by 2008; and
(b) if so, whether Government have
created required infrastructure for achieving
this target?
Misuse of Participatory Notes by
terrorists
*306. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the inflow of
Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs)
investment in the country are rising through
Participatory Notes (PN) routes;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is also a fact that some
terrorist mafia organizations are using the
Participatory Notes route in the country
and misusing such investments in the
Indian markets; and
(d) if so, the details of steps taken/
proposed to be taken against erring financial
institutes?
Financial crunch at HCL
*307. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES
AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the financial crunch that the Hindustan
Cables Limited in Andhra Pradesh is facing;
(b) whether it is a fact that employees
are also not being paid their salaries
regularly;
(c) whether the State Government of
Andhra Pradesh has requested his Ministry
to persuade Ministry of Communications
and Information Technology for some
orders of cables, etc.;
(d) if so, what the Ministry has done in
this regard;
(e) whether IIT, Kharagpur, proposed
for taking up some diversification activities
of HCL; and
(f) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons for the Ministry not approving the
same?
Motor fuels under VAT
*308. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have received representation from oil
industry for bringing motor fuels under VAT
as this will enable to reduce the burden of
flaring crude prices on common man;

98
(b) whether it is also a fact that the VAT
regime will enable to rationalise the varying
State taxes; and
(c) if so, by when it is expected to be
implemented?
Missing watermark instrument from
Nasik Security Press
†*309. SHRI AJAY MAROO:
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:

watermark instrument used in printing of
postal stamps, judicial and non-judicial
stamp papers, passports and cheque books
and other material of State Bank of India at
Central Government's Security Press,
Nasik has gone missing;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action Government are taking in

Projected capacity in airlines sector
2262. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether travel industry estimates
project passenger growth for airlines sector
at 250 per cent over the coming five years
whereas capacity growth will be around
350 per cent for the same period;
(b) if so, whether this will result in gross
overcapacity forcing the air carriers to raise
their unremuneratively low fares; and
(c) whether in such a scenario, the
national carrier Indian should concentrate
on profitability rather than market share as
it did for the current fiscal year making a
net profit of Rs. 68.00 crores?
Merger of Indian and AI
2263. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
had taken a decision to retain its holding in
the new airlines after the merger of Indian
and Air India;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the new
airlines will consider special business units
that should become the real profit centres;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Reduction in base price of
jet fuel
2264. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry has taken up
with the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural
Gas and all oil PSUs to impress upon them
to reduce the base price on fuel;
(b) if so, whether the Ministry has
received a positive response from State-
owned oil firms to cut the base price of jet
fuel;
(c) whether Indian, which is facing
pressure from falling fares, is also seeking
lower taxes on jet fuel, which makes up
nearly 30 per cent of a carrier's operating
cost; and
(d) if so, by when a final decision in this
regard is likely to be taken?

525
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Growth in Aviation Sector
  2265. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether India will need nearly 1,500
to 2,000 aircrafts in the next 10 years with
air travel expected to grow at an average
rate of 25 per cent in the time period and
procuring these aircrafts is estimated at
$ 75 billion;
(b) whether, at present, there are more
than 10 million people flying everyday and
Government are proposing that this number
will increase to 100 million in a few years;
and
(c) if so, what is the strength at present
and the steps taken to procure the required
number of aircrafts?
Hijack threat by terrorists
†2266. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that terrorists
have threatened to hijack aeroplanes;
(b) if so, the details of such information
received by Government;
(c) whether any special action plan has
been prepared by Government for the
security of the aeroplanes flying out of the
country; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Merger of Indian and
Air India
2267. SHRI SHANTARAM
LAXMAN NAIK:
SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the much talked-about
merger of Indian and Air India has taken
place;
(b) if so, the essential features of the
agreement;
(c) the benefits, if any, that passengers
travelling by the air services of the two
companies are going to derive;
(d) whether employees have agreed to
the merger; and
(e) the details referring to the safeguard
of employees, stipulated, if any, in the
agreement?
Expert Committee to make Indian
profitable
2268. SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE:
SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether any Expert Committee has
been constituted by Government to
formulate strategies to make Indian
profitable;
(b) if so, the names of the members of
the Expert Committee;
(c) whether the Committee has
submitted any report; and
(d) if so, the details of the
recommendations?

526
Special air-package
2269. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE
THAKUR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
introduce special air-package in Himachal
Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir in view
of the potential for tourism; and
(b) if so, by when the special air-package
is likely to be introduced in these States?
Use of Haj Terminal at IGIA
2270. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
propose to use the Haj Terminal situated
at IGI Airport in New Delhi for domestic
services during non-Haj time;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of steps Government have
